skill.name: higgsfield-product-photoshoot
skill.description: Create product photoshoot image jobs through Higgsfield CLI for studio, lifestyle, ad, hero, carousel, model, and restyle visuals.
skill.summary: Generate product photoshoot images with Higgsfield modes and structured interview guidance.
skill.author: higgsfield-ai

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, mode names, placeholder URLs, and sample output. The confirmed risks are the curl pipe to sh installer, external Higgsfield CLI execution, and intentional upload of local image files to a backend service. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to sh.
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic curl pipe to sh guidance. Link to installation instructions, require explicit user approval, and document checksum or signature verification.

remediation.issue: CLI commands use user-derived prompt and image values.
remediation.suggestion: Require safe argument quoting and reject shell metacharacters in prompt, path, and aspect ratio values before running Bash commands.

remediation.issue: Local image paths are auto-uploaded to an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users that images will be uploaded to Higgsfield and ask for confirmation before submitting local files.

remediation.issue: Examples rely on remote service output without privacy guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that generated URLs and uploaded assets may be processed or hosted by Higgsfield according to its service terms.

content.value_statement: Product teams need high-quality product images for stores, ads, and campaigns. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through Higgsfield modes to create focused photoshoot jobs.
actual_capabilities: Selects from product_shot, lifestyle_scene, hero_banner, carousel, ad pack, model tryout, conceptual, and restyle modes.
Asks up to four labeled questions to clarify count, style, placement, audience, and reference images.
Runs the Higgsfield product-photoshoot create command for selected modes.
Supports local image paths or existing upload UUIDs as image references.
Returns final image URLs and avoids exposing internal prompts or job metadata.
limitations: Requires the Higgsfield CLI and a logged-in Higgsfield account.
May require installing a remote CLI before use, which needs user review.
Does not write raw GPT Image 2 prompts because the backend assembles them.
Uploads provided local image files to Higgsfield for processing.

use_cases.title: Launch Store Images
use_cases.description: Create clean studio or lifestyle images for ecommerce product pages and launch collections.

use_cases.title: Produce Campaign Assets
use_cases.description: Generate coordinated ad variants, carousel slides, or hero banners for paid and owned channels.

use_cases.title: Restyle Product Visuals
use_cases.description: Refresh existing product photos with seasonal, aesthetic, or mood changes while preserving the product.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Studio Shot
prompt_templates.scenario: A user has one product image and needs simple ecommerce photos.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three clean studio product photos for this uploaded bottle. Use a white background and keep the label readable.

prompt_templates.title: Lifestyle Scene
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants social content with the product in use.
prompt_templates.prompt: Make lifestyle images of this coffee can on a sunlit kitchen counter for Instagram. Use a warm morning mood.

prompt_templates.title: Campaign Pack
prompt_templates.scenario: A marketer needs multiple connected ad assets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create five paid social ad variants for this skincare product. Use a premium wellness look and emphasize hydration.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Restyle Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: A brand team needs seasonal reuse of an existing image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Restyle this existing product image for a holiday campaign. Keep the product unchanged and use quiet luxury styling with warm gold accents.

output_examples.input: User uploads a candle photo and asks for a Pinterest pin.
output_examples.output: The skill selects moodboard_pin, asks for count and aesthetic, then returns the ready image URLs.

output_examples.input: User asks for a website banner showing a product in use.
output_examples.output: The skill selects hero_banner, gathers the missing style details, and returns the final banner image links.

output_examples.input: User provides an existing product image and asks for a Christmas version.
output_examples.output: The skill selects restyle, preserves the product subject, and returns the seasonal image results.

best_practices: Upload a clear product reference image before asking for generated photos.
State the channel, format, and mood so the skill can choose the correct mode.
Confirm that local files may be uploaded before running the Higgsfield command.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for raw text-to-image requests without a product context.
Do not bypass the product-photoshoot command by calling a generic image model command.
Do not ask it to reveal backend prompts, internal IDs, or hidden model instructions.

faq.question: Does this skill require a product image?
faq.answer: A product image is preferred for better fidelity. Text-only requests are possible but may be less accurate.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Can it create ad creatives?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an ad_creative_pack mode for coordinated static ad variants.

faq.question: Can it make a virtual model wear a product?
faq.answer: Yes. The virtual_model_tryout mode is intended for products worn or used by an AI-rendered model.

faq.question: Does it expose the generated prompt?
faq.answer: No. The skill says the backend assembles prompts and the final response should only include image URLs.

faq.question: What should users review before use?
faq.answer: Users should review the Higgsfield CLI install step, account login, and any local image upload.
